page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz. The instance is configured with 256 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance and high PassMark memory scores, placing the instance in the top tier for these metrics. However, multi-core CPU performance and cached small-block memory read bandwidth align with average mid-range expectations. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in uncached large-block memory operations, where both read and write bandwidth fall into the lower performance tier. For language processing, the instance demonstrates strong text generation speeds with small models, while medium-sized model inference remains average.

Given its high memory density and dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.r7a.8xlarge offers a resource profile suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The qualitative cost efficiency is favorable for applications requiring large in-memory datasets but moderate multi-core compute scaling. Appropriate workloads include in-memory databases, caching layers, enterprise applications, and memory-bound data processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server featuring 32 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM, it delivers 256 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs, but provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks highlight strong single-core CPU capabilities and high PassMark memory scores, contrasted by weaker uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth. This profile makes the instance highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications that benefit from dedicated CPU resources and a large memory footprint without requiring local SSD storage.
